plan.title: What Is Entropy?
plan.description: Entropy explains why ice melts, why rooms get messy, and why time only runs one way. This video unpacks the physics of disorder using probability and real examples.

beats.narration: Drop a hot iron into cold water and the iron cools down. But the water never spontaneously heats the iron back up. Why does nature only run one way?

props.clip_query: hot iron dropped into cold water
clip_queries: hot iron dropped into cold water
steam rising from hot water surface
props.alt: steam rising from a hot liquid surface

beats.narration: The answer is entropy. It is a measure of how many microscopic ways energy can be arranged inside a system. More arrangements means higher entropy.

props.definition: A measure of how many microscopic arrangements of particles and energy are possible for a given state of a system.

beats.narration: Picture a drop of ink in water. At first the ink is clumped together. Then it spreads out until it is fully mixed. Spreading out reaches equilibrium.
The clumped state has very few arrangements. The mixed state has an astronomically larger number. Nature drifts toward the most probable state, every single time.

props.label: Possible particle arrangements in a mixed state vs. just one for the p

beats.narration: Ludwig Boltzmann captured this in one equation: entropy S equals Boltzmann's constant times the natural log of W, where W is the number of microstates.

steps.note: S: entropy, k_B = 1.381×10⁻²³ J/K, W: number of microstates

beats.narration: The second law of thermodynamics says entropy in an isolated system never decreases. Every spontaneous process moves toward higher entropy, never lower.

props.text: Entropy never decreases in an isolated system.

beats.narration: That is why heat flows from hot to cold. The change in entropy equals heat transferred divided by temperature. Hot-to-cold transfer always produces a net gain.

steps.note: Heat Q added at temperature T always increases total entropy

beats.narration: And it is why some processes are irreversible. Ice melts, gases expand, and mixed liquids do not unmix, because returning to the ordered state is overwhelmingly unlikely.

props.clip_query: ice melting in a glass of water
clip_queries: ice melting in a glass of water
gas expanding in a container simulation
liquids mixing together in a beaker
props.alt: ice cube melting slowly in a glass

beats.narration: This one-way drift from ordered states to mixed states, from low entropy to high, is what physicists call the arrow of time.

events.label: Ordered state: all molecules in one place
Equilibrium: highest entropy, no net change

beats.narration: So entropy is not just disorder. It is probability made physical. The universe tends toward the states that can be arranged the most ways, and that tendency shapes everything we see.
